lens: Warren Sack — recursive social systems (fictional analytical lens)
readerSummary: The current portfolio makes a repeatable method legible: listen to relationships and friction, make a model, shape an interface or workflow, use it with people, and preserve what is learned for the next participant or maintainer. The three explicit About loops can be reconstructed from case-study evidence without treating the lab proposal or historical coursework as deployed work.

evidence: The About page names three loops and links them to Harry J. Epstein, FairRentNYC, and Sunday Dinner / 196.
HJE's Listen → Frame → Implement → Verify → Continue specimen identifies customer/team friction, scoped requirements, shared incremental releases, stakeholder checks, and maintained patterns.
FairRentNYC connects listening meetings and ballots to documents, public campaign pathways, collective use, and sustained follow-through.
The two Sunday Dinner / 196 reconstructions expose the operating sequence through discussion, space preparation, independent use, minimal documentation, and continued support.
About states: 'observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document enough for others to continue.'
The heading 'Systems people can inhabit' was reached through one desktop click and two mobile actions. The current links lead to the projects used in the three-loop trace.
WOWList turns organizers' own language into followable keyword communities and distribution workflows, with public support/adoption evidence and shared authorship.
CallNYC turns administrative records into recognizable resident issues, district context, and next steps; its original launch screenshot and linked public implementation provide a tangible interface.

The commercial and participation specimens let a reader connect what was learned to reusable patterns and handoffs. The coalition sequence ties web architecture to physical meetings and public action.
CLM-SOCIAL-INFO-SPACES-PROTOTYPE remains a held projection with no public surfaces and is absent from the redacted public registry.
The About limits expressly reject structural-equivalence proof and current technical proficiency from historical implementation evidence.
CallNYC is visibly archived, independent, and non-current. WOWList identifies the present return as a threshold rather than a restored calendar.

The lab calls its two-week engagement proposed and its acceptance conditions unproven; it rejects finished-platform and client-adoption claims. The Maven certificate is separately framed as professional development.
No raw faculty testimonial or protected educational-record wording was found on the rendered routes reviewed.
This scorecard is one independent score of 4. It cannot establish the three-judge median or the no-score-below-3 condition.

threeProjectTrace.interface: The team implements incremental public storefront/content/commerce changes; a dated public storefront capture is visible.
threeProjectTrace.socialUseAndRevision: Jamie inspects the public customer path and reviews operational or analytical signals with stakeholders; About names refinement through customer and team use.

threeProjectTrace.limits: The specimen is a reconstruction from the governed public claim set, not an original internal workflow or proof of every historical release. The project dates remain 2009-2015.

threeProjectTrace.interface: Maintained campaign sites, action paths, practical sessions, hearings, and town halls; public screenshots make the web interface inspectable.
threeProjectTrace.socialUseAndRevision: The case describes ballots, working sessions, shared campaign alignment, public participation, and ongoing follow-through across many collaborators.
threeProjectTrace.documentationAndHandoff: Running minutes, source maps, question logs, action trackers, and 30+ pages of shared memory let collaborators recover context and continue.
threeProjectTrace.evidence: Current rendered screen/working-session/public-room sequence, implementation citations, and bounded operating narrative.

threeProjectTrace.observe: Artist proposals, video discussions, hospitality, returning participants, and practical needs of a shared space.
threeProjectTrace.model: Proposal review, onboarding, configuration, access handoff, invitations, responses, and follow-up form the participation workflow.
threeProjectTrace.interface: Artist-residency handoff and the recurring invitation/gathering workflow operate as social interfaces.
